part-0-opening.q: According to the Freeman et al. meta-analysis of 225 studies, active learning raised exam performance by about how much?
part-0-opening.why: Freeman et al. (PNAS, 2014): about 0.47 standard deviations, in undergraduate STEM courses.

part-0-opening.q: What is the rule for using AI in this workshop's first exercises?
o: AI writes the first draft, you correct it
Human draft first, AI second, and you decide
Use AI only after the workshop
part-0-opening.why: Human draft first (Exercises 1 to 11). AI second. You decide: every AI line gets a human verdict.

part-1-foundations.q: In C4 terms, what is a container?
o: Something that runs, such as an application or a data store
part-1-foundations.why: A container is a runtime thing you start. It is not necessarily Docker.

part-1-foundations.q: What did the 2026 ETH Zurich study find about auto-generated agent context files?
o: They had no effect at all
They only helped on large repositories
They tended to lower success and raise cost by over 20%
part-1-foundations.why: Auto-generated files tended to lower success and raised cost by over 20%. Write only what the code cannot tell, and keep it short.

part-2-1-goals.q: Which statement makes a quality goal testable?
o: 95% of order confirmations appear within 3 s at 300 orders per minute
The app must be easy to use
part-2-1-goals.why: A scenario with a number can be verified. Adjectives like fast and secure cannot.

part-2-1-goals.q: Why limit your top quality goals to three to five?
o: The template only has five boxes
You cannot maximise everything, and focus drives the architecture
Quality goals are optional after five
part-2-1-goals.why: A very fast system and a very cheap one are built differently, so you choose.

part-3-2-constraints.q: A client says: You must host in our own datacentre. What is it, usually?
part-3-2-constraints.why: It is imposed from outside and limits your choices, so it belongs in section 2.

part-3-2-constraints.q: Which answers the three-question test as a constraint?
o: Negotiable: yes. Imposed: no. Limits choices: no
Negotiable: yes. Imposed: yes. Limits choices: no
Negotiable: no. Imposed: no. Limits choices: yes
Negotiable: no. Imposed: yes. Limits choices: yes
part-3-2-constraints.why: No, yes, yes: it is a constraint.

part-4-3-context.q: What belongs in the context diagram?
o: The system as a black box, and everything that exchanges information with it
Only the people who use the system
part-4-3-context.why: Internal components are out of scope here and belong in section 5.

part-4-3-context.q: Which interface-table column do most teams skip, and which causes incidents?
part-4-3-context.why: Failure behaviour is the row most teams skip and the one that causes incidents.

o: Quality goals and constraints to building blocks
part-5-4-strategy.why: Quality goals and constraints lead to the strategy, which leads to building blocks.

part-5-4-strategy.q: Which strategy statement is specific rather than generic?
o: Idempotency key on every write request
part-5-4-strategy.why: If a neighbour can guess something specific from your table, it is specific enough.

o: A statement that is always true
A condition that must be true before a call
An error returned to the caller
part-6-5-building-blocks.why: An invariant is always true. A pre-condition holds before a call and an error mode describes a failure.

part-6-5-building-blocks.q: How many building blocks should Level 1 roughly have?
o: As many as there are classes
part-6-5-building-blocks.why: Fewer than 4 may hide structure. More than 12 probably mixes levels.

part-7-6-runtime.q: What does the runtime view show?
o: How building blocks interact over time in a scenario
part-7-6-runtime.why: Structure shows what exists. Runtime shows how it behaves.

part-7-6-runtime.q: Which is a common mistake in section 6?
o: A failure branch with a visible outcome
A caption saying what to notice
Participants that do not exist in section 5
part-7-6-runtime.why: Participants must be section 5 blocks or neighbours.

part-8-7-deployment.q: What is the key table in the deployment view?
o: A mapping from each building block to a node
part-8-7-deployment.why: Every block appears in the mapping table.

part-8-7-deployment.q: What does the deployment view's pipeline sketch show?
o: Build, test and deploy in four or five boxes
part-8-7-deployment.why: Sketch the pipeline (build, test, deploy) in 4 or 5 boxes.

part-9-8-crosscutting-concepts.q: When does something belong in section 8?
o: When it affects exactly one block
When it is a technology brand
When it affects two or more blocks
When it is a legal rule only
part-9-8-crosscutting-concepts.why: If only one block is affected, put it in section 5.

part-9-8-crosscutting-concepts.q: What does a well-written concept include?
o: Name, rule, where it applies, why and a link
part-9-8-crosscutting-concepts.why: Name, rule, where it applies, why, link. Name the pattern, not a tutorial.

part-9b-see-it-run.q: In Demo 3, a webhook is lost. What happens to the order?
o: It stays PendingPayment and later settles to Paid
part-9b-see-it-run.why: Unknown is not failed: the order stays pending until checked.

part-9b-see-it-run.q: What does it mean that docs and code check each other?
o: The code is generated from the diagrams
Tests fail if a named test does not exist
Nobody needs to review the documents
part-9b-see-it-run.why: A test fails if a named test does not exist, and a checker fails if an ID is used but never defined.

part-10-9-decisions.q: What should you do when a decision is reversed?
o: Mark the old ADR superseded and write a new one that links back

part-10-9-decisions.q: Which consequence list would you trust in an ADR?
o: Survives outages; adds one component to operate
part-10-9-decisions.why: A good ADR names a real cost.

part-11-10-quality-requirements.q: Which are the three kinds of scenario?
Which scenarios should you design for now?
part-11-10-quality-requirements.why: High on both: design for it now. Low importance, high difficulty: question the requirement.

part-12-11-risks-and-12-glossary.q: What is the difference between a risk and technical debt?
o: Debt is future and risk is past
A risk might go wrong; debt is a shortcut already taken that must be repaid
part-12-11-risks-and-12-glossary.why: Both belong in section 11 and both need an owner.

part-12-11-risks-and-12-glossary.q: A risk with no owner is...
part-12-11-risks-and-12-glossary.why: Every risk needs someone who watches it.

part-13-ai-lab.q: In the lab, what verdicts can each AI line receive?
o: Accepted, rejected or edited, with a reason
part-13-ai-lab.why: Every AI line gets a verdict. The reasons are the learning.

part-13-ai-lab.q: Which are the three red-team lenses?
part-13-ai-lab.why: Borrowed from research on multi-agent LLM failure modes (Cemri et al., NeurIPS 2025).

part-14-agents-as-readers.q: What did the 2026 research suggest about agent context files?
part-14-agents-as-readers.why: The shared headline: short, specific and human-written.

part-14-agents-as-readers.q: Why pair every don't with a do instead?
part-14-agents-as-readers.why: Give the agent an alternative to follow.

part-15-close.q: What links a goal to a test, per the golden thread?
Which section holds your numbered constraints?
part-15-close.why: Section 2, numbered so other sections and tools can cite them.
